findings.message: Within the entrance-ceremony recollection, the surrounding English alternates between past and historical-present narration. P56 uses present tense (‘I look down and let out a small sigh’) after P53/P55 establish past narration. Review whether this is an intentional historical-present shift or should be made consistent.

P59 uses past tense (‘I heard an incredibly cute voice’) immediately after P56 uses present tense in the same entrance-ceremony recollection. Review the paragraph against the intended narrative tense for this continuous scene.

P60 switches back to present tense (‘I glance toward the voice’) directly after P59 uses past tense (‘I heard’). Review whether the tense shift is intentional or should be made consistent with the surrounding recollection.

P69 narrates the angel smiling and walking away in past tense while nearby parts of the same entrance-ceremony recollection use present-tense narration. Review it against the intended tense frame for the scene.

P72 switches to present tense (‘I instinctively follow Shirasaka-san’s retreating figure with my eyes’) after P69 narrates the same continuous recollection in past tense. Review whether this shift is intentional or should be made consistent.

The English says Shirasaka-san is solving math problems with her eyebrows ‘furrowed into “八”.’ The Japanese character-shape shorthand is likely opaque to an English reader without explanation; consider rendering the worried/downturned eyebrow expression directly or otherwise making the image understandable.
